A woman in a blue top defends Ved for Ved's height and willingness to turn vegetarian. The caption calls it a return to LinkedUp, but the packet holds no earlier LinkedUp post to name.

DeBtte7sl5L.h: [[P080|The drones sketch]] opens Protest satire, with @anuj.mp4 as both the official and the aide, aiming surveillance tools at a women's safety punchline.
DeBtte7sl5L.r: A distorted face filter marks the official and the plain face the aide, and the turn is the official telling women to dress properly instead of watching colleges. It is the first post in the entry, dated 3 Oct. The likes outran the comments, which fits a sketch with a point to make and nothing to debate.
DeBtte7sl5L.f: Likes kept climbing after day 7 while comments stayed level, a stretch that overlaps the week of [[P092|the 'Utha lete hain' reel]] and the CJP story, though nothing shows viewers arriving from one to the other.

DeEn-wDMsEy.h: [[P081|The waist-size argument]] is @anuj.mp4 recording parents on a hotel vacation, a family-room reel with no scripted turn.
DeEn-wDMsEy.r: The mother calls out the recording in the first seconds, so the camera is known and the family plays to it. The joke runs on whether the waist is 30 or 40 inches, then on an admission that the father called the mother a sumo wrestler, ending on a pan to the father. The voices come from family, not @shreeecreates or a collaborator.

DeHUp_3jNfA.h: [[P082|The 'noir' set]] mixes black-and-white suit portraits with photos of the on-set monitors, with no joke attached.
DeHUp_3jNfA.r: Stills alternate between polished portraits against windows and a car and warm monitor playback, one showing a pew with two other actors, which points to a shoot for something else. The photographer is credited in the caption. Photo posts here do better with a text hook, as the quote cards in [[P037|the Iconic quotes carousel]] did.

DeGpclKMoBd.h: [[P083|The 'artsy people' clip]] is a party montage captioned as an infiltration, with no spoken line to carry it.
DeGpclKMoBd.r: The joke is the gap between the caption and the footage: wine glasses, a mock fight held back by two friends and foreheads slapped at a floral dining table, cut to rap. It sits in the Brand events and studios place with no brand named in the packet. Likes landed just ahead of usual and comments just behind, an ordinary result.

DeKXGzNMW_C.h: [[P084|The Don YG stream clip]] opens the Flex reels: @anuj.mp4 in the black Versace robe fans cash while Don YG plays unreleased tracks.
DeKXGzNMW_C.r: It is framed as a stream guest spot, and @anuj.mp4 closes by telling viewers that this is what joining the stream gets them. The robe and the cash echo [[P056|the brand-deal sketch]] from 16 Sep, where cash bundles first appeared on a bed. Don YG, the robe and the cash all carry into the next two days.
DeKXGzNMW_C.f: Likes kept climbing after day 7 on the first of the Flex reels, a late rise that nothing visible explains.

DeJ1xr6MGns.h: [[P085|The one-drink, ten-drink sketch]] splits @anuj.mp4 into a timid self and a bathrobe barfly, and the twist is that the drink was non-alcoholic.
DeJ1xr6MGns.r: Two brands share the post: a Sober rum and cola that turns out to be non-alcoholic, and a Fast&Up NightOut tablet handed over against hangovers. The robe from the Flex reels appears in a bar, and a line about being taller than Ved Maddison calls back to [[P079|the LinkedUp referral]]. Two brands and a long running time are confounds for the low likes and plays.

DeMDeApMaxp.h: [[P086|The 'brokies' lip-sync]] carries a paid label and still reads as a flex reel, with Don YG, chains and the robe in a bedroom.
DeMDeApMaxp.r: Fixed header text sets the joke and a rap audio about not tolerating broke people does the rest. Nothing in the execution reads as an ad, so the label is the only sign. It follows [[P084|the stream clip]] by a day with the same people and props, and it is the shortest of the three Flex reels.

DeMFFKQOgTy.h: [[P087|The briefcase reel]] closes the Flex reels with watches, cash and a lip-synced money track, and no on-screen text at all.
DeMFFKQOgTy.r: @anuj.mp4 opens a monogram case of luxury watches while a red-haired woman, filed under Don YG in the entries, fans 500-rupee notes, and both lip-sync a Hindi hip-hop verse. Where [[P086|the previous day's reel]] used a header line to set up the joke, this one trusts the props.

DePFfcmspTA.h: [[P088|The Rahul plea]] adds a new second voice, an elderly man in bed who delivers the warning slowly.
DePFfcmspTA.r: The setup matches [[P078|the Esha plea]] from a few days earlier, and both are about drinking. The turn is the camera swinging to the elder, whose one-line reason earns 'great argument' from @anuj.mp4. Comments held near usual while likes landed under, so this plea did not draw the comment lift the earlier ones did.

DeO0IQ_Gsbi.h: [[P089|The Matchday Hangout poster]] announces a Liverpool v Manchester City watchalong with @anuj.mp4 as one of six creators.
DeO0IQ_Gsbi.r: The poster is the whole post: JioHotstar and Star Sports YouTube, 11th Oct at 8:30 PM, footballers and creators cut out on blue. It starts the account's run of Premier League posts, followed by the studio photos and the trophy visit. Likes landed a little under usual and comments close to it.

DeSGnTuDJ0N.h: [[P090|The 'make instagram casual again' pair]] is two photos of @anuj.mp4 with three friends, liked far more than discussed.
DeSGnTuDJ0N.r: A front selfie and then a view from the floor looking up, under a caption about friends meeting after a long time. The comment gap fits the shape: no question, no named person to tag and no spoken line, as with the other casual photo dumps such as [[P025|the 'jeene mein aye maza' dump]]. Followers rose across its first two days, a window shared with [[P091|the Amazon game reel]].

DeR095fszsD.h: [[P091|The Amazon price game]] is a stream-format sketch where @anuj.mp4 loses round after round, and the plays ran far past the likes.
DeR095fszsD.r: The hook is six seconds of disbelief at an iPad price, and the black-and-white WASTED stamp repeats as a running gag. The caption carries the Great Indian Festival tags and the Amazon handle, which marks it as brand work even without a paid label. The same gap showed on [[P075|the Crime Patrol phone ad]]; what drives it is not visible.

DeTodI2sZGF.h: [[P092|The 'Utha lete hain' reel]] sets how the government treats protesters against how it treats rapists, and it set the account's best likes and comments since tracking began.
DeTodI2sZGF.r: One repeated line flashes over names of public critics, then the frame goes black and white and a coy voice invites rapists to join the party. The caption ties it to the CJP protest, which [[P094|the next day's commentary]] shows was a live story, and it is the second Protest satire reel after [[P080|the drones sketch]]. Followers rose 1,796 that day against a typical 127, with no way to credit the post.

The caption names the broadcaster and league handles, so this is the brand visit shown, not performed, with no joke or sketch. Followers rose over its first two days alongside two other posts, so none can be credited.

It went up the day after [[P092|the 'Utha lete hain' reel]] on the same story, so the likes cannot be separated from that wave.

Without that reference the clip is a cashier quoting a price. Plays ran under usual.

The tone is closer to [[P060|the Tourette story call]] than to the arguing calls. It put the Shree calls back above usual after [[P076|the Good knight review]] broke the run.

DebcI8wscbi.h: [[P097|The menu skit]] is a silent restaurant performance about government defenders, and it was liked and discussed far beyond what its plays suggest.
DebcI8wscbi.r: @anuj.mp4 argues with a beverage menu, tosses it and clutches the forehead over a rap track, with no spoken line. The header line about 'andhbhakts' and the caption about the 13 crore deleted votes supply the politics, so the viewer brings it. It sits in the Protest satire entry, which was three in a row above usual before it.
riding: the Protest satire run: 3 in a row above usual before it

It leans on lip-sync more than the talking pieces before it, such as [[P097|the menu skit]]. The day-3 read is early, but the entry is on a run, which is the nearest explanation for it.
riding: the Protest satire run: 4 in a row above usual before it

The tier-list shape was used before in [[P054|the Revolutionaries ranking]], and the car setting returns from [[P074|the Ronaldo and Messi skit]]. Day-3 numbers are early.

Dejc5cUjM8r.r: Slides take in a suit portrait, a tattooed hand with rings, a baby-bib film set, a Persian cat and a streaming desk, so the money props of [[P087|the briefcase reel]] and the football thread share one carousel. Comments sit low, as on other dumps like [[P025|the 'jeene mein aye maza' dump]]. Day-3 numbers are early.

DemG3EgsFOx.h: @anuj.mp4 lets Gemini plan the Garba night, then breaks the plan on one fact only the character could supply.
DemG3EgsFOx.r: The brand tool solves a problem the character made, as in [[P033|the Emergent sketch]], but the last beat turns on the venue's name, which neither @anuj.mp4 nor the assistant has. Plays ran far past likes here as on [[P075|the Crime Patrol phone ad]]; the paid label and #ad tag are the one visible confound, and plays say nothing about unique viewers.

DeowPIlsWag.h: [[P104|The old money parody]] has @anuj.mp4 pose in gold satin pajamas around the house and beside a Rekha poster.

The robe-and-sunglasses persona from [[P084|the Don YG stream clip]] and [[P087|the briefcase reel]] returns without the cash, so wealth is a costume here, not a flex. Day-1 numbers are early.

DeoWbCns0La.r: A black-and-white 90s montage, graphic cards on CEO pay and the stock market, and a pivot to the Solana Summit India in Mumbai on the 2nd of November. It comes at money from the other side of [[P068|the salary screenshot]]: the system failed the employee. Day-1 numbers are early.

DerFPnBB35E.h: A Nykaa Wanderlust review that says 'brand deal' out loud, and the lowest likes since tracking began.
DerFPnBB35E.r: @anuj.mp4 plays a streamer addressing 'chat' while parents heckle off-screen, and the line 'let me do my brand deal in peace' admits the ad inside the bit, though no paid label shows. Comments held far better than likes, and it is the third brand post in a row under usual, so the pattern predates this one. Family voices return from [[P081|the waist-size argument]].

Earlier the car was a prop in [[P050|the Bombay dump]] and a destination in [[P061|the Tanjore Ride Along]]. Day-3 numbers are early.

The dispute invites viewers to take a side, which may explain the early lean to comments, though that stays a guess. No paid label shows, yet the caption and closing card read as a product plug.

The strangers do the work: they huddle, shout and point on the beat, so no cash or robe is needed. It is the mood of [[P087|the briefcase reel]] without the watches. Day-3 numbers are early.

De1o8UPhQc9.r: The grammar matches [[P073|the Nikita complaint]]: a handheld daylight selfie, the name in a header, Ruhee Dosani stepping in beside @anuj.mp4. The turn is a stool pun, 'would you like to sit on my... chair?', then a song. Where [[P078|the Esha plea]] scolds, this one courts, so the plea format now runs both ways. Day-3 numbers are early.

De3g9DhhiM9.h: Ved Maddison plays the uninvited guest on Day 1 in Japan, a trip vlog where every stop gets a deadpan comment.
De3g9DhhiM9.r: 'Ved what the hell, I told you not to come' sets the running gag, and the route runs from a family breakfast through pachinko, Akihabara arcades and graded Pokémon cards to street skewers. Ved Maddison walked into [[P030|the Admirin' You piano cover]] and became the target of [[P079|the LinkedUp referral]]; here the role is the friend who won't leave. Day-3 numbers are early.

De1LDHWAbqd.h: One frame beside a Sriracha vending machine is the Japan trip's postcard.
De1LDHWAbqd.r: No joke and no speech: tinted sunglasses, baggy trousers and a machine stocked with hot sauce under the only text, 'SRIRACHA JAPAN'. The object is the gag. It sits between [[P112|the Day 1 vlog]] and [[P114|the yen reel]] as the quiet frame, and thin comments are the usual outcome for single stills here, as with [[P025|the 'jeene mein aye maza' dump]]. Day-3 numbers are early.

De4FQCWh5VJ.h: The Flex reels reach Tokyo, with a stack of yen where the rupee cash used to be.
De4FQCWh5VJ.r: The caption's '4 peti' is the line from [[P087|the briefcase reel]], and holding the stack as a phone is a new gag on the cash-fanning of [[P084|the stream clip]]. A friend in a kimono and white face paint and the neon street supply the Tokyo costume. It is the first Flex reel since the three on 6 and 7 Oct. Day-3 numbers are early.
riding: the Flex reels run: 3 in a row above usual before it

De6CpXpgZEp.h: A silent Shibuya night dump that carries the yen prop into stills.

Slide 9 has @anuj.mp4 holding yen notes over the face, the prop of [[P114|the yen reel]] posted the same day. Comments sit low early, as on [[P102|the 'kuch tasveerein' dump]]. Both sketches close on 'Sneakers, but better' and a Rohit, which makes [[P109|the couples-therapy sketch]] the template. Day-1 numbers are very early.

DcVwMLsDJhk.h: Far under usual on likes; lowest comments on record.
DcVwMLsDJhk.r: Three portraits next to a carved mask in red candlelight, credited to a photographer. Nothing happens across the slides, and comments barely moved.

DcYnia_MAFM.h: Just under usual on likes, comments above usual.
DcYnia_MAFM.r: @anuj.mp4 begs a friend with folded hands to stop sending Instagram baddies. One shot, one line of text, and comments ran ahead of likes.

DcYKISTDPME.r: Twenty slides of group-chat roasts among @anuj.mp4 and friends, with no caption. It runs long and uncurated, with no single line to carry it.

DdOLjMfjDEr.h: Day 1: likes and comments just above usual.
DdOLjMfjDEr.r: Quote cards on diamonds, phone batteries and a self-made line, in the same black and gold frame. Day 1 is just above usual, so no call yet.
